prompt: A ratio table has $3 \to 21$ and $? \to 49$. What is the missing input?
hint: This time the output is known and the input is missing, so you will need to work backward. First find the rule from the complete pair.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Sketch a tape diagram: equal blocks for each part. What does one block represent here?
This time the output is known and the input is missing, so you will need to work backward. First find the rule from the complete pair.
Since $21 \div 3 = 7$, each output is $7$ times its input. Undo that multiplication for $49$ by working out $49 \div 7$.

explanation: Find the multiplier from the complete pair: $21 \div 3 = 7$, so outputs are $7$ times inputs.
To go from an output back to its input, use the opposite operation and divide by $7$.
Carrying out the division gives $49 \div 7 = 7$ for the input.
The missing input is $7$, and the check $7 \times 7 = 49$ confirms it.
